fields.description:
> **THIS TICKET WAS FILED ON A FALSE PREMISE AND HAS BEEN REWRITTEN.** The original description
> claimed `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` asserts conditions a `# mechanism-ok:` marker
> cannot affect, and therefore that the ratchet forbids ALL new mechanisms. That was WRONG. Both
> assertions DO honour markers — one is `assert "new=0" in out or "admitted" in out`, the other is
> `assert set(baseline) | admitted == live`, where `admitted` is exactly the marker-admitted set.
> A correct marker satisfies both. The false claim cost change 2601 a design restructure and cost
> another story its env-var tier. What follows is the corrected, much narrower ticket.

## The real defect: silent non-admission

A `# mechanism-ok:` marker that does not match a detected mechanism key is **silently ignored**.
The mechanism stays unadmitted, the gate fails, and nothing tells the contributor that their
marker was parsed but matched nothing. `scripts/_mechanism_delta/compare.py:95` requires a marker
for the **exact** key, so a marker that is well-formed but attached to the wrong key — or placed
where the detector does not look for that key's shape — behaves identically to no marker at all.

The failure the original ticket recorded was real:

```
FAILED tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py::test_check_passes_on_the_committed_tree
  - AssertionError: active=682 new=1 increased=0 stale=0
  - Extra items in the right set: 'ci_gate::scripts/check_bare_repository_discovery.py'
```

But the cause was not "markers do not work". It was that THAT marker was not admitted, and the
contributor had no way to see why. The diagnosis cost was the whole defect.

## Why placement is genuinely easy to get wrong

`ci_gate` has TWO detection shapes and they do not take a marker in the same place:
- a gate script, keyed by PATH (`ci_gate::scripts/check_*.py`)
- a workflow `run:` step, keyed by `file::step`

A contributor who knows the marker syntax but not which shape their mechanism is detected as will
place it correctly-by-syntax and wrongly-by-key, and get silence.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A `# mechanism-ok:` marker that matches NO detected mechanism key produces a
      diagnostic naming (a) the marker as parsed, (b) the key it was interpreted as, and (c) the
      keys actually detected nearby. Silence on an unmatched marker is the defect; the diagnostic
      is the fix.
- [ ] AC2 — Reproduce change 2601's exact marker and determine why it was not admitted. If it is a
      parser or placement defect, fix it; if the marker was genuinely wrong, document the rule that
      makes it wrong. Either outcome is acceptable — an unexplained "it should have worked" is not.
      NOTE: the retraction comment's original proof cited the scanner-integration workflow's two
      `ci_gate` markers, but that workflow has since been REVERTED and is absent from main. That
      proof is STALE and the reproduction must be re-derived from 2601 itself or from a
      constructed equivalent.
- [ ] AC3 — `docs/architecture.md` §"Mechanism-delta ratchet" states marker placement PER
      DETECTION SHAPE, explicitly covering both `ci_gate` shapes (script-by-path and
      workflow-step-by-`file::step`).
- [ ] AC4 — Defect-seeded: a deliberately malformed or mis-keyed marker makes AC1's diagnostic
      fire. A test that cannot distinguish the diagnostic from its absence does not pin AC1.

## Non-goals

NOT changing the ratchet's shrink-only semantics, NOT weakening the "new mechanism fails the
build" rule, and NOT opening a contributor path to edit `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` or run
`--update-stale` — those remain maintenance-only and correctly closed. The marker is and remains
the sanctioned route; this ticket only makes its failure mode legible.

## Concurrency note

file_impact overlaps `AGENTS.md` with ticket 0d6c and `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` with
ticket 7f46. Must NOT be worked concurrently with either.
